extracted.intended_audience: public relations and investor relations professionals; press release writers and corporate communicators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for formatting press releases so they are readable, media-friendly, and more likely to get coverage. Focuses on headline, length/style, structural elements, boilerplate, contacts, and multimedia attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline that grabs attention
rubrics_metrics.description: How to write a headline that grabs attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong headline is essential to engaging readers and media; it should grab attention and summarize the news succinctly so the story stands out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideal length and style for readability
rubrics_metrics.description: The ideal length and style for readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concise, readable language and an appropriate overall length so the release is easy to scan and understand; readability boosts media attention and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of subheadings, bullet points and quotes effectively
rubrics_metrics.description: How to use subheadings, bullet points and quotes effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure content with subheadings for hierarchy, bullet points for key facts, and quotes to add voice or authority—these elements improve scannability and storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting is as important as content (clear, well-structured release)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formatting your press release correctly is just as important as the content. A clear, well-structured release makes your news more engaging, grabs media attention and helps your story shine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize clarity and structure throughout the release (logical flow, visual hierarchy, short paragraphs) because good formatting increases the likelihood of pickup by media and readability by audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a boilerplate 'About' paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Include an 'About' section describing the company or organization (e.g., 'About Notified').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise boilerplate that explains who you are, your positioning, and any relevant corporate affiliations—this standard closing helps reporters and readers understand the issuer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide media contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Include media contact details (name, email, and optionally phone/agency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List a clear media contact (example: 'Caroline Smith - Caroline.smith@icrinc.com') so journalists can follow up for interviews or additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include accompanying multimedia/attachments (photos)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide links to accompanying multimedia (e.g., 'A photo accompanying this announcement is available at [URL]').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach or link to images, videos, or other assets to increase story appeal and make it easier for media to use the content; include accessible URLs for downloads.
